Hi Vivek / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're ready to start the integration and want to lock down the cutover plan and SDK guidance so our platform team can schedule the migration. Quick asks to help us scope: 

- Do you have a short Node + Go quickstart we can run in our staging? Prefer a tiny sample that shows auth, idempotency, and stream handling.
- Recommended default timeouts and retry/backoff you support for token-level calls (esp. long-poll streaming).
- Clarify endpoint migration mechanics: will our DNS change or is this an API key switch? Any warm-up/burst guidance?
- During the cutover we plan a ~2 hour bulk transform where we replay ~120k requests(); what rate limits should we expect and can we request a temporary bump?

AppCircle

Sam — great to hear you're ready. High level plan and next steps below; attaching a mutual action plan so we can populate cutover windows and responsibilities. Also linking our public SDK quickstart in the Drive.

Short answers up front:
- Quickstarts: we have minimal Node + Go examples that cover auth (API key + optional mTLS), idempotency tokens, and graceful streaming. I'll have Prio (cc) attach runnable samples.
- Timeouts/retries: start with a 15s request timeout for standard calls, 120s for streaming; retry with full-jitter exponential backoff starting at 300ms, max 6 retries for idempotent requests. Non-idempotent POSTs: avoid automatic retries at the client layer; instead use idempotency keys.
- Cutover: no DNS changes required. We support a staged API-key flip and also a routing tag so you can send a percentage of traffic to the new endpoints while keeping the old key active for rollback. For bulk replay we recommend a ramp (10m ramp to target rate) and an initial soft cap at 60% of your expected peak, then manual bump.
- Rate-limit bump: we can request a temporary burst via our Capacity team; please complete the attached rate-limit request form with desired per-second and per-minute targets.

Action items:
1) Sam/Anna: fill the mutual_action_plan.xlsx with your desired cutover window and target TPS by July 18.
2) Vivek/Prio: provide the sample zip and a short stability checklist.
3) Monica: coordinate CS/Impl support during the cutover (we should schedule a 2-hour war-room).

Attaching: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (template), sdk-quickstart-links.docx (links).

Thanks — Vivek
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Hi Sam — Prio from the platform team here. I put together a couple of runnable samples and a short checklist. Attaching: sdk-node-samples.zip and sdk-go-example.md. Below are the core recommendations we use in production.

1) Auth and client init (Node):
- Use API key in Authorization: Bearer <key>. For added security, enable mTLS on the client side if your infra allows.
- Example header set: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer <key>', 'X-Request-Id': '<uuid>', 'X-Idempotency-Key': '<uuid-if-needed>' }

2) Retry and timeout policy (recommended defaults):
- Non-stream calls (idempotent GETs, safe retries): timeout = 15s, retry = 5 attempts, backoff = jittered exp( base=250ms, factor=2, max=5s ).
- Streaming/generation calls: timeout = 120s per chunk, do NOT auto-retry streaming sessions end-to-end; instead implement reconnect with resume token logic.
- Non-idempotent writes: do NOT auto-retry; require client-generated idempotency-key for server-side dedup.

3) Exponential-backoff snippet (pseudo-Node):
- const backoff = (attempt) => Math.min(5000, 250 * Math.pow(2, attempt)) + Math.random() * 100;
- on 429 or 5xx, wait backoff(attempt) before next try. Abort after max attempts.

4) Rate-limit handling:
- 429 response includes headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (epoch sec). Prefer adaptive throttling: reduce concurrency when Remaining < 10%.
- For bulk migration: do a 10-minute warm-up with linear ramp to target TPS. Use a token-bucket on client side to avoid bursts.

5) Cutover checklist (short):
- Create test API key and run 10k calls across Node/Go samples against staging.
- Validate idempotency keys for bulk writes.
- Confirm monitoring hooks: set up per-route latency and error alerts in our Console.
- Schedule 2-hour war-room and give our Capacity team the filled rate-limit form 72 hours before cutover.

If you want I can paste a runnable Node script inline; I attached the zip with two examples (auth, streaming resume, backoff).

— Prio
Software Engineer, Integrations | Redwood Inference

Sam / Anna — thanks for the quick turnaround and for returning the forms. Confirming the operational picture and next steps: 

- Burst behavior: by default requests that exceed configured quota will receive 429s (we do not queue long-running customer requests at the gateway). During your cutover we can provision a temporary burst policy that raises per-route limits for a 6-hour window covering your migration. That policy will be applied to your API key and is per-route.
- Headers to use: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (reset is per-route). We also return Retry-After when applicable.
- Routing to Dedicated: we can route traffic to a Dedicated pool if you opt into a short-term Dedicated burst (requires a signed SOW). If you want that path, sign the attached SOW (DocuSign link below) and we'll open the Dedicated lane.

Next steps and owners:
1) Redwood (Vivek): request Capacity to apply a temporary burst for Aug 8 — done after we receive signed SOW.
2) AppCircle (Sam/Anna): sign SOW if you want Dedicated lanes; otherwise we will provision the per-key burst policy.
3) Monica: schedule 2-hour war-room + Slack channel for Aug 8 09:00–11:00 PT.
4) Prio: drop a short monitoring runbook (alerts and console queries) in the Drive folder.
